findings.title: Cursor decoder accepts noncanonical JSON property order
findings.evidence: JSON.stringify(parsed) === source rejects whitespace and duplicate-key spellings, but JavaScript preserves input property insertion order. A valid compact cursor with keys reordered is therefore accepted although encodeReviewInboxCursor emits only {v,actor,scope,createdAt,id}. This does not bypass actor/scope binding or project grants, but it falls short of the acceptance requirement for canonical cursors.
findings.minimal_correction: After validating fields, require the decoded source to equal JSON.stringify({ v: parsed.v, actor: parsed.actor, scope: parsed.scope, createdAt: parsed.createdAt, id: parsed.id }) or require the submitted token to equal encodeReviewInboxCursor(parsed). Add a reordered-key rejection test.

reviewed_criteria: Authenticated fixed-role developers and approvers, explicit current project grants, bootstrap-empty response, active-project and organization scoping, three scopes, and requester exclusion for approver eligibility.

Fixed 25-row plus one pagination; bounded summary fields with no plan items/SQL, source content, target profile, credential reference, or repository path projection; exact microsecond timestamp wire values and descending (created_at,id) keyset order.
Context-bound cursor actor/scope/time/id checks, malformed/oversize/invalid-UTF8 rejection, per-page membership recheck, and stable behavior after revocation.
Inbox loading/empty/error states, filters, refresh/load-older, exact existing plan navigation, draft clearing, scope and sign-out stale-response guards, and denial cleanup.

Real PostgreSQL fixtures for foreign/archived/revoked scopes, both roles, requester exclusion, tied microsecond order, API recreation, complete populated state snapshots, and browser stale scope/navigation/signout/revocation paths.
License and dependency boundary: no changed license, notice, dependency manifest, or lockfile in the diff from the stated base.
